items.answer: Down group 2 each atom has more electron shells, so the atomic radius grows and the outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded. The attraction on the outer electrons weakens, so they are lost more easily to form M2+ ions, and reactivity rises down the group.

items.answer: Chlorine is a stronger oxidising agent than bromine and iodine, so it displaces bromide (forming orange Br2) and iodide (forming brown I2). Iodine is the weakest oxidising agent of the three, so it cannot displace chloride. Oxidising power falls down group 17.
